dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: They're up against us, the Shogunate army, you know? Those inferior rebels aren't gonna hold out much longer, just you wait.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You appear to be very confident in yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Of course, our army is well-equipped and highly motivated. There are many veterans like me here who know how to fight wars.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Those disorganized Sangonomiya militiamen lack discipline. Naturally, they are no match for us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Don't worry, you can trust me. I mean, how could the Shogunate possibly lose?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's the war going at the moment?

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Well, about that... We've fought them so many times. Though they are inferior to the Shogunate army in terms of manpower and equipment, they are still relentless and are putting up a desperate fight.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: As for what we should do next exactly, we should probably follow the orders of the higher-ups. You can't just fight and kill all the time. Regrouping and recreation are also necessary aspects of war.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Don't get the wrong idea. I'm not saying that because I'm afraid of them.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: All wars have their casualties. Even though we're on the winning side, there will still be unseen scars left on people.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: For a commoner like you, it's best that you stay far away from this hellhole.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you can tell me about this area?

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: What? Are you still thinking of traveling around here even though you know there's a war going on? You've really got guts...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: As you can see, Kannazuka is the location of the Shogunate camp. It's run by the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Southwest of Kannazuka is Tatarasuna. Jade Steel, Inazuma's pride and joy, is produced there. However, there was an accident at the Mikage Furnace recently, so you probably should find a detour.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: If you keep heading west, you'll find yourself on Yashiori Island. That's where the rebel camp is. I've heard that those scoundrels were trying to hire more men. Don't you get taken in by them!

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Yashiori Island also contains the corpses of slain gods and demons. It's got that spectacular valley created by the Electro Archon with her serpent-slaying sword going for it, though! So if you do really travel there, you have to go pay that place a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: I've heard about the Tatarigami running amok near those remains, though, so it's better that you don't go there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about "Masanori" ...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: That guy is dead.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: He swordsmanship was top notch, and he and Kenji Kazumichi were both well-liked by our superiors. How could he just defect like that? I really don't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: If it wasn't for this ridiculous incident, Kenji wouldn't have...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Alas, poor Kenji. That kid shouldn't have become like that...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Have you heard? The Shogunate and Sangonomiya have agreed to a ceasefire.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Looks like I'll finally get to go home soon...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Haha, just kidding. It's just a short ceasefire. I doubt I'll be going anywhere anytime soon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the ceasefire...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: To be honest, I was relieved when I heard about the ceasefire.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: But don't get the wrong idea, though. It's not like I'm afraid of those small fry from Sangonomiya or anything. We're still the stronger party when it comes to military might by a long shot!

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: It's just that I'm past the age where you're all hot-blooded and up for a fight, you know? I'm beginning to think that it's not good for people to remain on the battlefield for too long.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: But of course, that doesn't mean that I'll go easy on anyone in a real fight.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: It can still be pretty dangerous around here, ceasefire notwithstanding, so best you be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you can tell me about this area?

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: As you can see, Kannazuka is the location of the Shogunate camp. It's run by the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Head southwest and you'll eventually reach Tatarasuna. Jade Steel, Inazuma's pride and joy, is produced there.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: If you go further west, that's Yashiori Island, territory of the Sangonomiya resistance.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Yashiori Island also contains the corpses of slain gods and demons. It's got that spectacular valley created by the Electro Archon with her serpent-slaying sword going for it, though! So if you do really travel there, you have to go pay that place a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: I've heard about the Tatarigami running amok near those remains, though, so it's better that you don't go there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about "Masanori" ...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: That guy is dead.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: His swordsmanship was top notch, and he and Kenji were always both well-liked by our superiors. How could he just defect like that? I really don't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: If it wasn't for this ridiculous incident, Kenji wouldn't have...

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Alas, poor Kenji. That was just unfortunate...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Matsudaira
dialogues.text: Aye, goodbye.
